newsitem.title: USA: Fed must look beyond current U.S. data - Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Fed must look beyond current U.S. data - Greenspan.

text.p: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan acknowledged on Thursday that inflation was benign but stressed that the central bank must look ahead, given delays in the effects of any interest-rate changes.
"The state of inflation at this particular stage is clearly under control," Greenspan said in response to a question during testimony to Congress' Joint Economic Committee.
But he added that given the lags between monetary policy actions and their effects on the economy and inflation, "We have to look beyond the current state of affairs."
"It's very hard to find any evidence of a mushrooming inflationary set of pressures at this point," the Fed chief said.

"What we at the Federal Open Market Committee are going to have to judge, however, is not so much the question of where prices are or have been. Rather, what is the state of the economy later this year and into 1998 when any actions we may or may not take would become effective?" he said.

Referring to the upcoming policymaking Federal Open Market Committee's meeting on March 25, Greenspan said the panel's discussion will be a "fairly detailed" one in which it will be important to get the perspectives of the 12 Federal Reserve bank presidents on the state of the economy in their various regions of the country.
"They have more recent data than anything that's published and that's been very useful for us in the past and I assume it will be continue to be useful to us in the future," Greenspan said.
Questioned about the relationship between growth and inflation, Greenspan said that low inflation was a "necessary condition" of maximum sustainable growth.
"We do not distinguish the goals of maximum sustainable economic growth from low inflation," he said.
